title: An 18.61-year term gave no clear ten-year sea-level forecast gain at 19 PSMSL gauges for 1980-2015 origins
abstract: We tested whether a fixed 18.61-year term improves annual mean sea-level forecasts in the tenth year after issue. We used a fixed cohort of 19 PSMSL gauges and 684 station-year targets at 1980-2015 origins. Each fit used the previous 60 calendar years. Adding a free sine and cosine term to a linear trend reduced mean squared error by 3.96%. The conditional 95% ten-origin block interval was -6.34% to 10.51%. RMSE fell from 49.95 to 48.95 mm. Equal weights for four occupied spatial cells changed skill to -0.22%, with limits of -6.96% to 5.89%. These results do not establish a forecast gain. They do not test the absence of a physical lunar effect. A small survivor cohort, strong regional concentration, revised source data, simple models and about two target cycles limit inference. The package contains code, source hashes, aggregate losses, resamples, an independent fit audit and a figure. External source records and record-level forecasts remain outside the signed package.

display.caption: Forecast MSE reductions and conditional 95% ten-origin block intervals, with network RMSE by issue year. All models use the same 19 gauges and prior 60-year windows.
